To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce a robust version of PCA, called UPCA, which can handle data that has been corrupted by permutations; 2) we show that UPCA is algebraically well-defined; and 3) we propose a two-stage algorithmic framework for UPCA.

(a) UPCA is a new problem of fundamental interest in data science, (b) we establish the well-posedness of UPCA, (c) we propose an efficient algorithmic pipeline for the problem, and (d) we demonstrate the potential of UPC for applications in data privatization and linkage.

(i) we establish the well-definedness of a fundamental problem in unsupervised learning, (ii) we propose the first practical algorithmic pipeline for this problem, (iii) we demonstrate the potential of our algorithmic pipeline in real-world data, and (iv) we provide a comprehensive set of experiments on synthetic and real-world data that validate our claims.

the problem of robust principal component analysis (PCA) from a data matrix whose columns have been corrupted with permutations.
developing a new robust statistical model for data analysis and developing efficient algorithmic tools for solving this model.
the fundamental question of how to perform principal component analysis on a dataset in which the entries in some of its columns have undergone a permutation.
